analysis.summary: Claudio puts the Claude Code CLI behind a REST API and a web UI (also a Linux desktop app and a PWA), so you can start, watch and answer Claude Code chats from anywhere, run agents in parallel through orchestrations, and rotate between several Claude accounts. It is for developers who already use Claude Code and want it as a long-running service they can reach from a browser, a phone or HTTP. It reaches Claude Code only through the CLI's program interface (stream-json, control requests, flags, transcripts) and is a Claude-only fork of Agentry.
implemented: REST API (Fastify, 39 route files) with OpenAPI 3.1 served by Scalar at /docs and /openapi.json; POST /api/chats starts a chat with prompt, cwd, worktree and jsonSchema; /chats/:id/messages, /stop, /interrupt, /resume, /fork, /permissions/:requestId and /chats/:id/stream exist as routes

Chats driven through `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json` with --resume when the process is gone; permission prompts, AskUserQuestion and plan approval answered from the UI; interrupt, switching permission mode and model mid-chat; attachments; per-chat git worktrees; --max-budget-usd cost limits
Global SSE feed at GET /api/events with Last-Event-ID resume that keeps the UI fresh without polling

Orchestrations: a task DAG run by parallel workers in their own git worktrees, merged on an integration branch, with a verification phase, optional pull request, resume, templates and a second engine that runs the graph as a Claude Code workflow

Several Claude accounts, each with its own CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR signed in once; usage per window, proactive rotation at a threshold, a turn that hits its limit replayed on the next account, waiting for reset only when no account has quota; a `claudio-accounts` CLI in packages/accounts
Changes reviewed inside Claudio: diffs of a chat, task or branch built from git and the transcript, with the sentence Claude wrote before each edit

Projects with a Tasks board (work items with per-project keys, five columns, epics, milestones), a team of Claude Code agent files and a flow by column that starts a role's run when a card enters a column; only a person moves a card to Done

Guards: PreToolUse hooks that hold even in bypassPermissions (no push, no --no-verify, no recursive delete outside the worktree, no secret written), plus an optional review gate on an orchestration's integrated diff

Authentication none, bearer token (only the SHA-256 stored) or OIDC JWT validation; read-only mode; audit log of writes; CLAUDIO_AUTH_MODE, CLAUDIO_AUTH_TOKEN and CLAUDIO_AUTH_TOKEN_RESET variables; in the Docker image a first-run owner token is printed once
Schedules (cron expression and time zone, overlap policy, missed slots recorded as skipped), usage and cost over time from the cost the CLI reports, and export of transcripts as Markdown or JSON

Packaging: Linux desktop app (Electron, .deb and AppImage, scripts/install.sh), Docker image ghcr.io/yeyo11/claudio with a Compose file and TLS profile, a Helm chart under deploy/helm, and a PWA with Web Push

Collaborators: read-only project sharing peer to peer over iroh; Tailscale serve tunnel; a terminal per project and chat (off by default); claude.ai connectors listing; a global Claudio assistant over Claudio's own MCP server
Interface in English and Spanish, Night Shift design system with dark and light themes
planned: ROADMAP.md says 'Nothing is planned right now'; there is no announced feature list beyond what was decided against
Revisit a native mobile shell or app-store packaging only if push on the installed PWA proves unreliable
Revisit per-user push only once a real per-user model exists
Revisit Flatpak/Snap packaging, offline use and a browser OIDC login flow only if there is demand (all currently 'decided against, for now')
documentedOnly: ROADMAP.md lists 'An apt repository of our own' under 'Decided against', but scripts/install.sh, the README and docs/decisions/apt-repository.md describe and use a signed apt repository; the roadmap entry is stale

ROADMAP.md says only the cost limit exists as a CLI flag and the time limit is Claudio's own clock, which is fine, but README's line 'whatever the CLI can do, Claudio can do' is broader than the code: claude.ai web artifacts and chat memory, and plugin/connector servers in a per-chat MCP selection, are not reachable
docs/status.md counts (1,578 source files, 557 test files, 90 browser specs, 33 roadmap areas) are snapshots that I did not re-verify, so they are not used in the announcements
limitations: Authentication is off by default for a source install or the desktop app; only the Docker image makes an owner token on first start. There is a single credential for everyone who holds it, no per-user isolation or permissions
Claudio does not terminate TLS; put a TLS-terminating proxy in front before exposing the port
OIDC mode only validates a JWT; there is no browser login flow
Only Claude Code runs today; other providers are described in docs/providers.md but not implemented
The desktop app is Linux x86_64 only; the Docker image is amd64 only
The desktop app runs on your machine with your own claude login, nothing sandboxed, and chats start in acceptEdits
Workers do not survive a restart: a task caught by one is marked interrupted and its chat continues in a new execution; what lives only in a live stream (stderr, the rate-limit notice) is lost
Usage rotation reads what the CLI ships; an idle account's usage is only as fresh as its last refresh, and a running claude is never moved to another account, only the next launch
Cancelling a single command needs Linux (/proc)
Web Push needs a secure origin and does not work in the Linux desktop app; a push subscription belongs to an install, not a person
A subscription token is meant for individual use; use an API key for anything shared
Version 0.9.0, pre-1.0; Claudio is an independent project and not affiliated with Anthropic

en.title: Claudio: run Claude Code as a service
en.description: Claudio puts the Claude Code CLI behind a REST API and a web UI, runs agents in parallel in their own worktrees and rotates between Claude accounts. Here is how it works and what it cannot do.
en.markdown:
Claude Code lives in a terminal. That is fine until you want to start a chat from your phone, check on an agent that is still working while you are away from the desk, or run five of them in parallel without losing track of which one needs an answer. I built Claudio to cover that gap: it runs Claude Code as a service.

This post covers what Claudio is, how it talks to Claude Code, how to install it, and, because it is a 0.9 release, what does not work yet.

## What you get

Claudio puts the Claude Code CLI behind a REST API and a web UI. The same server also backs a Linux desktop app and an installable web app for your phone. Everything runs on your machine or your server, with your own Claude login.

- Chats you can start, stream and answer from a browser or over HTTP.
- Orchestrations: a graph of tasks run by parallel workers, each in its own git worktree.
- Several Claude accounts, with work moving to the one that still has quota.
- A review screen for what the agents changed.
- Projects with a task board and a team of agents.

I will go through them one at a time.

## The one rule: only the interface the CLI ships for programs

Claudio does not scrape the terminal, call undocumented endpoints or log in a second time on its own. It reaches Claude Code through the CLI's flags, its stream protocol and the files it writes. [docs/cli-surfaces.md](https://github.com/yeyo11/claudio/blob/main/docs/cli-surfaces.md) lists every surface in use, one row per need. For example:

```text
Run / continue a conversation  claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json
Auth status                    claude auth status --json
Session history                $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/*/*.jsonl
```

The practical consequence is a ceiling: what the CLI cannot do, Claudio cannot do. Web artifacts and claude.ai chat memory have no CLI surface, so Claudio does not touch them.

## Chats over HTTP

A chat is one long-lived `claude` process fed over stdin, with `--resume` when the process is gone. You can start one from the UI or from the API:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8797/api/chats \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt": "Add a unit test for parseDuration", "cwd": "/workspace/my-app"}'
```

The request also accepts `worktree` (run inside a new git worktree of that name) and `jsonSchema` (structured output). From there you have `POST /api/chats/:id/messages`, `/stop`, `/interrupt`, `/resume` and `/fork`, and `GET /api/chats/:id/stream` to follow it. When the agent asks for permission, a question or a plan approval, you answer from the UI (or `POST /api/chats/:id/permissions/:requestId`).

The interactive reference is served at `/docs` and the OpenAPI 3.1 document at `/openapi.json`. If you turned authentication on, send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

The UI does not poll. One server-sent events feed, `GET /api/events`, carries chats, prompts waiting for you, tasks, orchestrations and account rotation, and it resumes with `Last-Event-ID` after a drop.

## Orchestrations

An orchestration is a graph of tasks. Workers run in parallel, each in its own git worktree, and their branches are merged into one integration branch. After that, a verification phase runs your checks (build, tests) on the integration branch under a timeout, and a pull request can be offered. It exists as the `POST /api/orchestrations` route and as a screen where you follow the run as steps.

Two things to watch for: the checks need `worktree: true` on the graph engine, and workers do not survive a restart. A task caught by one is marked `interrupted` and its chat continues in a new execution while it has attempts left.

## Several accounts, rotated

Each Claude account gets its own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and is signed in once. Claudio reads usage per window, moves new work to an account with quota before a limit is hit, replays a turn that hits its limit on the next account, and waits for the reset only when none has any quota left. There is also a small CLI, `claudio-accounts`, in `packages/accounts`.

Limits: a running `claude` is never moved to another account, only the next launch is. And an idle account's usage is as fresh as its last refresh, because the CLI offers no event for it.

## Reviewing changes inside Claudio

For a chat, a task or the integration branch there is a diff screen built from git and the transcript. Each edit carries the sentence Claude wrote just before it, so you read the change together with its reason.

## Projects, a board and a team

You can import a directory as a project. It gets a Tasks board with work items (`AGN-12`-style keys, five fixed columns, epics, milestones), and a team where each member is a Claude Code agent file with a role. With the flow switched on, a card entering a column starts that role's run. Only you move a card to Done.

## Guards

Claudio can add `PreToolUse` hooks that hold even in `bypassPermissions`: no push, no `--no-verify`, no recursive delete outside the worktree, no secret written. They are on for orchestration workers and the flow, and configurable per project for chats. The mechanism is a settings file with only Claudio's hooks, passed with `--settings`. See [docs/guards.md](https://github.com/yeyo11/claudio/blob/main/docs/guards.md).

## Install

**Docker** (amd64):

```bash
docker run -d --init --name claudio --restart unless-stopped -p 127.0.0.1:8797:8797 \
  -v claudio-config:/home/node/.claude -v claudio-data:/data -v claudio-workspace:/workspace \
  ghcr.io/yeyo11/claudio
```

Open `http://localhost:8797`, sign in with the owner token the container printed once (`docker logs claudio`), then sign in to Claude in the setup assistant. Name all three volumes, or replacing the container to update starts again with empty ones.

**Desktop app** (Linux x86_64, `.deb` or AppImage):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yeyo11/claudio/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

As with any script piped to a shell, read it first. The app runs with your own `claude` and `~/.claude` login, so nothing is sandboxed and chats start in `acceptEdits`.

**From source** (Node 22+, pnpm 10, a logged-in `claude` on your `PATH`):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yeyo11/claudio && cd claudio
pnpm install
pnpm dev          # API on :8797, UI on :5181
```

Then: open Claudio, let the setup assistant check Claude Code, press New chat, pick a directory and write a prompt.

## Before you expose it

A container creates an owner token on its first start. A source install or the desktop app has authentication off until you turn it on. That is right for a port bound to `127.0.0.1` and wrong for anything else: with auth off, anyone who reaches the port can start a chat on your account and read every transcript on the machine. The modes are `none`, `token` (only the SHA-256 is stored) and `oidc` (Claudio validates a JWT; it does not log anyone in). Claudio does not terminate TLS, so put a proxy in front. [docs/securing.md](https://github.com/yeyo11/claudio/blob/main/docs/securing.md) has the details.

## What does not work yet

- One credential for everyone who holds it: no per-user isolation or permissions.
- Claude Code is the only provider that runs. The docs describe what a provider is, but there is no second one.
- The desktop app is Linux x86_64, the image is amd64.
- Web Push needs a secure origin; it does not work in the desktop app, and a subscription belongs to an install, not a person.
- Cancelling a single command needs Linux, because it reads `/proc`.
- It is version 0.9.0. Expect rough edges.

Claudio is a Claude-only fork of Agentry, an independent project, and is not affiliated with Anthropic.

## What comes next

The roadmap says nothing is planned right now. What is left was decided against for now, with reasons: native app-store shells, per-user push, offline use, a browser login flow for OIDC. If one of those matters to you, open an issue and tell me why.

The code is MIT-licensed at [github.com/yeyo11/claudio](https://github.com/yeyo11/claudio).

es.title: Claudio: Claude Code como servicio
es.description: Claudio pone la CLI de Claude Code detrás de una API REST y una interfaz web, ejecuta agentes en paralelo en sus propios worktrees y rota entre cuentas. Cómo funciona y qué no hace todavía.
es.markdown:
Claude Code vive en una terminal. Está bien hasta que quieres iniciar una conversación desde el móvil, mirar cómo va un agente cuando no estás en tu mesa, o lanzar cinco en paralelo sin perder la pista de cuál necesita una respuesta. Hice Claudio para cubrir ese hueco: ejecuta Claude Code como un servicio.

En este artículo cuento qué es Claudio, cómo habla con Claude Code, cómo se instala y, como es una versión 0.9, qué todavía no funciona.

## Qué te da

Claudio pone la CLI de Claude Code detrás de una API REST y una interfaz web. El mismo servidor sirve a una app de escritorio para Linux y a una web instalable en el móvil. Todo corre en tu máquina o en tu servidor, con tu propio login de Claude.

- Conversaciones que puedes iniciar, seguir y responder desde un navegador o por HTTP.
- Orquestaciones: un grafo de tareas que ejecutan workers en paralelo, cada uno en su propio worktree de git.
- Varias cuentas de Claude, y el trabajo pasa a la que aún tiene cuota.
- Una pantalla para revisar lo que cambiaron los agentes.
- Proyectos con tablero de tareas y un equipo de agentes.

Las voy repasando una a una.

## La regla única: solo la interfaz que la CLI ofrece a los programas

Claudio no lee la pantalla de la terminal, no llama a endpoints sin documentar ni hace un segundo login por su cuenta. Llega a Claude Code por los flags de la CLI, su protocolo de stream y los ficheros que escribe. [docs/cli-surfaces.md](https://github.com/yeyo11/claudio/blob/main/docs/cli-surfaces.md) lista cada superficie en uso, una fila por necesidad. Por ejemplo:

```text
Ejecutar / continuar una conversación  claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json
Estado de autenticación                claude auth status --json
Historial de sesiones                  $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/*/*.jsonl
```

La consecuencia práctica es un techo: lo que la CLI no puede hacer, Claudio tampoco. Los artefactos web y la memoria de chat de claude.ai no tienen superficie en la CLI, así que Claudio no los toca.

## Conversaciones por HTTP

Una conversación es un proceso `claude` de larga vida alimentado por stdin, con `--resume` cuando el proceso ya no existe. Puedes iniciarla desde la interfaz o desde la API:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8797/api/chats \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt": "Añade un test unitario para parseDuration", "cwd": "/workspace/mi-app"}'
```

La petición también acepta `worktree` (ejecutar dentro de un worktree nuevo de git con ese nombre) y `jsonSchema` (salida estructurada). A partir de ahí tienes `POST /api/chats/:id/messages`, `/stop`, `/interrupt`, `/resume` y `/fork`, y `GET /api/chats/:id/stream` para seguirla. Cuando el agente pide un permiso, hace una pregunta o pide aprobar un plan, respondes desde la interfaz (o con `POST /api/chats/:id/permissions/:requestId`).

La referencia interactiva está en `/docs` y el documento OpenAPI 3.1 en `/openapi.json`. Si activaste la autenticación, envía `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

La interfaz no hace polling. Un único feed de server-sent events, `GET /api/events`, lleva conversaciones, avisos que esperan tu respuesta, tareas, orquestaciones y rotación de cuentas, y se reanuda con `Last-Event-ID` tras un corte.

## Orquestaciones

Una orquestación es un grafo de tareas. Los workers corren en paralelo, cada uno en su propio worktree de git, y sus ramas se integran en una rama de integración. Después, una fase de verificación ejecuta tus comprobaciones (build, tests) sobre esa rama con un tiempo límite, y se puede ofrecer una pull request. Existe como ruta `POST /api/orchestrations` y como pantalla donde sigues la ejecución por pasos.

Dos cosas a tener en cuenta: las comprobaciones necesitan `worktree: true` en el motor de grafo, y los workers no sobreviven a un reinicio. Una tarea que pilla uno queda `interrupted` y su conversación sigue en una ejecución nueva mientras le queden intentos.

## Varias cuentas, rotadas

Cada cuenta de Claude tiene su propio `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` y se inicia sesión una sola vez. Claudio lee el uso por ventana, pasa el trabajo nuevo a una cuenta con cuota antes de llegar al límite, repite en la siguiente cuenta un turno que choca con el límite, y espera al reinicio solo cuando ninguna tiene cuota. También hay una CLI pequeña, `claudio-accounts`, en `packages/accounts`.

Límites: un `claude` en marcha nunca se mueve a otra cuenta, solo el siguiente arranque. Y el uso de una cuenta inactiva está tan fresco como su última actualización, porque la CLI no ofrece un evento para eso.

## Revisar los cambios dentro de Claudio

Para una conversación, una tarea o la rama de integración hay una pantalla de diff construida a partir de git y de la transcripción. Cada edición lleva la frase que Claude escribió justo antes, así que lees el cambio junto con su motivo.

## Proyectos, tablero y equipo

Puedes importar un directorio como proyecto. Obtiene un tablero de Tareas con elementos de trabajo (claves tipo `AGN-12`, cinco columnas fijas, épicas, hitos) y un equipo donde cada miembro es un fichero de agente de Claude Code con un rol. Con el flujo activado, una tarjeta que entra en una columna inicia la ejecución de ese rol. Solo tú mueves una tarjeta a Hecho.

## Guardas

Claudio puede añadir hooks `PreToolUse` que se cumplen incluso en `bypassPermissions`: sin push, sin `--no-verify`, sin borrado recursivo fuera del worktree, sin escribir secretos. Están activos para los workers de las orquestaciones y para el flujo, y se configuran por proyecto en las conversaciones. El mecanismo es un fichero de ajustes con solo los hooks de Claudio, pasado con `--settings`. Mira [docs/guards.md](https://github.com/yeyo11/claudio/blob/main/docs/guards.md).

## Instalación

**Docker** (amd64):

```bash
docker run -d --init --name claudio --restart unless-stopped -p 127.0.0.1:8797:8797 \
  -v claudio-config:/home/node/.claude -v claudio-data:/data -v claudio-workspace:/workspace \
  ghcr.io/yeyo11/claudio
```

Abre `http://localhost:8797`, entra con el token de propietario que el contenedor imprimió una sola vez (`docker logs claudio`) e inicia sesión en Claude desde el asistente de configuración. Nombra los tres volúmenes; si no, al reemplazar el contenedor para actualizar empiezas con volúmenes vacíos.

**App de escritorio** (Linux x86_64, `.deb` o AppImage):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yeyo11/claudio/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

Como con cualquier script que se pasa a un shell, léelo antes. La app corre con tu propio `claude` y tu login de `~/.claude`, así que no hay sandbox y las conversaciones empiezan en `acceptEdits`.

**Desde el código** (Node 22+, pnpm 10 y un `claude` con sesión iniciada en el `PATH`):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yeyo11/claudio && cd claudio
pnpm install
pnpm dev          # API en :8797, UI en :5181
```

Después: abre Claudio, deja que el asistente compruebe Claude Code, pulsa Nuevo chat, elige un directorio y escribe un prompt.

## Antes de exponerlo

Un contenedor crea un token de propietario en su primer arranque. Una instalación desde el código o la app de escritorio tienen la autenticación desactivada hasta que la actives. Eso es correcto para un puerto ligado a `127.0.0.1` e incorrecto para cualquier otra cosa: sin autenticación, cualquiera que llegue al puerto puede iniciar una conversación en tu cuenta y leer todas las transcripciones de la máquina. Los modos son `none`, `token` (solo se guarda el SHA-256) y `oidc` (Claudio valida un JWT; no inicia sesión a nadie). Claudio no termina TLS, así que pon un proxy delante. [docs/securing.md](https://github.com/yeyo11/claudio/blob/main/docs/securing.md) tiene los detalles.

## Lo que todavía no funciona

- Una sola credencial para todo el que la tenga: no hay aislamiento ni permisos por usuario.
- Claude Code es el único proveedor que funciona. La documentación describe qué es un proveedor, pero no hay un segundo.
- La app de escritorio es para Linux x86_64 y la imagen es amd64.
- Web Push necesita un origen seguro; no funciona en la app de escritorio, y una suscripción pertenece a una instalación, no a una persona.
- Cancelar un comando concreto requiere Linux, porque lee `/proc`.
- Es la versión 0.9.0. Espera aristas sin pulir.

Claudio es un fork de Agentry solo para Claude, un proyecto independiente y sin relación con Anthropic.

## Qué viene

El roadmap dice que ahora mismo no hay nada planificado. Lo que queda se descartó por ahora, con sus motivos: shells nativos para las tiendas de apps, push por usuario, uso sin conexión, un flujo de login en navegador para OIDC. Si alguna de esas te importa, abre una issue y cuéntame por qué.

El código tiene licencia MIT en [github.com/yeyo11/claudio](https://github.com/yeyo11/claudio).

reddit.title: Claudio: self-hosted web UI and REST API for Claude Code (Docker, MIT)
reddit.body:
I run Claude Code on a server and got tired of SSH sessions to check on it, so I wrote Claudio: a REST API and web UI over the Claude Code CLI. MIT licensed, runs with your own Claude login.

Deploy:

```bash
docker run -d --init --name claudio --restart unless-stopped -p 127.0.0.1:8797:8797 \
  -v claudio-config:/home/node/.claude -v claudio-data:/data -v claudio-workspace:/workspace \
  ghcr.io/yeyo11/claudio
```

The image is non-root with the CLI pinned. The first start prints an owner token once (`docker logs claudio`). There is also a Compose file with a TLS-proxy profile and a Helm chart, and the app is installable as a PWA with Web Push on a phone.

Security, since it matters here: the container makes an owner token, but a source install or desktop app has auth off by default. Modes are none, bearer token (SHA-256 stored) or OIDC JWT validation. There is a single credential for everyone who holds it, no per-user permissions, and Claudio does not terminate TLS, so put a reverse proxy in front. With auth off, anyone reaching the port can start a chat on your account and read the transcripts. [docs/securing.md](https://github.com/yeyo11/claudio/blob/main/docs/securing.md) covers it.

Other limits: amd64 image, workers do not survive a restart (the task is marked interrupted and continues), Web Push needs HTTPS, and it is pre-1.0.

Write-up: https://josegarrido.dev/en/claudio-run-claude-code-as-a-service/?ref=reddit
Repo: https://github.com/yeyo11/claudio

reddit.title: Claudio: I turned the Claude Code CLI into a service with a REST API and web UI
reddit.body:
Claude Code only lives in a terminal, so I built Claudio to use it from anywhere. It puts the CLI behind a REST API and a web UI (plus a Linux desktop app and a phone-installable PWA) and adds what I kept wanting: parallel agents in separate git worktrees, a diff review screen, and rotation between several Claude accounts when one runs out of quota.

The rule I held to: only use what the CLI ships for programs (stream-json, flags, the transcripts it writes). That keeps it honest but caps it. If the CLI cannot do something, Claudio cannot either.

It grew into a lot more than I planned: a task board with work items, a team of agents with a flow by column, schedules, usage and cost over time. It is a Claude-only fork of an earlier project, Agentry.

What is not great yet: v0.9.0, a single shared credential with no per-user permissions, Linux and amd64 only for the packaged builds, and Claude Code is the only provider.

Write-up: https://josegarrido.dev/en/claudio-run-claude-code-as-a-service/?ref=reddit
Code (MIT): https://github.com/yeyo11/claudio

Feedback welcome, especially on what feels like too much.

reddit.title: Claudio (MIT): a REST API and web UI over the Claude Code CLI
reddit.body:
I released Claudio v0.9.0, an MIT-licensed project that runs the Claude Code CLI as a service: a Fastify REST API with an OpenAPI 3.1 document, a React web UI, and an Electron app for Linux.

The design constraint is written into CONTRIBUTING.md and CLAUDE.md: Claudio reaches an agent only through the interface its vendor ships for programs (CLI flags, the official SDK, a documented protocol, files the CLI writes). No terminal scraping, no undocumented HTTP endpoints. The table of every surface in use is in docs/cli-surfaces.md, and the docs folder doubles as the project's knowledge base: each feature and decision has a page.

It began as a fork of Agentry (0.37.1) that I narrowed to Claude Code only and renamed. Claudio is independent and not affiliated with Anthropic.

Open questions for contributors: a second provider is described in docs/providers.md but not built, and the roadmap lists what was decided against, with reasons (native app-store shells, per-user push, a browser OIDC flow). Commits follow Conventional Commits and release-please builds the changelog.

Write-up: https://josegarrido.dev/en/claudio-run-claude-code-as-a-service/?ref=reddit
Repo: https://github.com/yeyo11/claudio

en.subject: Claudio 0.9.0: Claude Code as a service
en.previewText: A REST API and web UI over the Claude Code CLI, with parallel agents and account rotation. What it does and what it does not.
en.markdown:
Hi,

I have been using Claude Code from a terminal for a long time, and I kept wanting to start a chat from my phone, see which agent was waiting on me, and keep working when one account ran out of quota. Claudio is what I built for that, and v0.9.0 is the first time I am presenting it properly.

It puts the Claude Code CLI behind a REST API and a web UI. It runs agents in parallel in their own git worktrees, shows you a diff of what changed, and moves work to another Claude account before a limit. It only uses the interface the CLI ships for programs, so it is as capable as the CLI and no more.

It is also pre-1.0: one shared credential, no per-user permissions, authentication off on a source install until you turn it on, and Claude Code as the only provider. The article spells those out next to the install commands for Docker, the Linux desktop app and a source checkout.

[Read the article](https://josegarrido.dev/en/claudio-run-claude-code-as-a-service/?ref=newsletter)

If you try it and something breaks, reply to this email or open an issue.

José Antonio

es.subject: Claudio 0.9.0: Claude Code como servicio
es.previewText: Una API REST y una web sobre la CLI de Claude Code, con agentes en paralelo y rotación de cuentas. Qué hace y qué no.
es.markdown:
Hola,

Llevo mucho tiempo usando Claude Code desde la terminal y siempre echaba de menos poder iniciar una conversación desde el móvil, ver qué agente estaba esperándome y seguir trabajando cuando una cuenta se quedaba sin cuota. Claudio es lo que construí para eso, y la v0.9.0 es la primera vez que lo presento como se merece.

Pone la CLI de Claude Code detrás de una API REST y una interfaz web. Ejecuta agentes en paralelo, cada uno en su propio worktree de git, te enseña el diff de lo que cambió y pasa el trabajo a otra cuenta de Claude antes de llegar a un límite. Solo usa la interfaz que la CLI ofrece a los programas, así que llega hasta donde llega la CLI y no más.

También es una versión previa a la 1.0: una sola credencial compartida, sin permisos por usuario, autenticación desactivada en una instalación desde el código hasta que la actives, y Claude Code como único proveedor. El artículo lo explica junto a los comandos de instalación para Docker, la app de escritorio para Linux y el código fuente.

[Lee el artículo](https://josegarrido.dev/es/claudio-claude-code-como-servicio/?ref=newsletter)

Si lo pruebas y algo falla, responde a este correo o abre una issue.

José Antonio
